evidence.title: Evidence-Based Language Learning
evidence.intro: The method behind Expatly isn't something we just made up — it's grounded in established second-language-acquisition research and in what actually works, again and again, in my own teaching.

stats.title: Your brain
stats.text: Shadowing activates your speaking center (Broca's area) far more than plain listening, which only uses your comprehension center (Wernicke's area). That's why you can read the menu but freeze the second you have to talk to the waiter. In my own lessons I see it firsthand: learners who shadow for 15 minutes daily speak noticeably more fluently within a few weeks.

stats.title: The grammar
stats.text: While your mouth is speaking, your brain quietly locks in grammar patterns along the way — no rule tables required. Linguist Shuhei Kadota describes exactly this effect: grammar is learned through use, not through drilling (Kadota, 2019).

stats.title: Your confidence
stats.text: Speaking isn't just a skill problem — it's a fear problem. Research on shadowing shows learners don't just improve, they genuinely enjoy speaking more. I see the same thing with my own students: the fear fades once the mouth has already said the words a few times.

evidence.closing: Not grammar tables. Not perfect scores. Just you, speaking — without the fear standing in your way.

sources.text: Kadota, S. (2019). Shadowing as a Practice in Second Language Acquisition: Connecting Inputs and Outputs. Routledge.

about.title: About Jonas
bio: I'm Jonas – passionate about languages and convinced that you don't just learn a language in your head, but above all with your mouth. I teach German – and if your language level makes something tricky, I'll help you out in English or Spanish, so nothing gets lost in translation.

I know firsthand how big the gap is between "studying a language" and "actually speaking it." That's exactly why my lessons aren't built on more theory, but on real sentences and conversations you actually need in daily life.
Together with my team, I've built a social media reach of over 1,000,000 followers. With Expatly, we follow one clear idea: Stop studying. Start speaking.
In my 1:1 online lessons, I help you speak German more naturally, more spontaneously and with more confidence – whether that's daily life, work, the doctor, paperwork or small talk.

items.a: The lessons are for learners from A1 to C1 – from absolute beginners to advanced learners who want to sound more natural and confident. Just message me on WhatsApp and we'll look at your current level together to find the plan that fits you.

You message me on WhatsApp or by email. We'll talk briefly about your current level, your goals, and where you freeze when speaking. After that, you get a clear recommendation for the training that fits you — from A1 to C1.
Yes, all lessons take place online — from home or on the go, via video call. All you need is a stable internet connection.

items.q: Which languages can the lessons be taught in?
items.a: Lessons are in German. If your language level makes something tricky, I'll help you out in English or Spanish, so nothing gets lost in translation.

items.q: How is this different from normal German lessons?
items.a: We do not just go through the next grammar lesson. The focus is on real sentences, direct feedback and situations you actually need in daily life.
You repeat real German sentences out loud until they come easily. This trains pronunciation and your feeling for natural language.

items.q: I'm afraid of making mistakes. Is that a problem?
items.a: No. That is exactly what the lessons are for. You get correction, but in a way that does not make you freeze. The goal is not perfection, but more confidence when speaking.

items.q: How fast will I notice progress?
items.a: That depends on your level and how much you practice. But many learners notice after a few sessions that they react faster and translate less in their head.

items.q: How quickly does Jonas respond to messages?
items.a: I usually respond within 24 hours – by email or directly on WhatsApp.

items.q: What time zone do you teach in?
items.a: I teach in Central European Time (CET/CEST). We simply coordinate a time that works directly over WhatsApp.

items.q: Are there group courses or a Speaking Club?
items.a: Yes, a German Speaking Club is planned. If you are interested, feel free to let me know on WhatsApp.
